title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
title_zh: 关节、相机、开拍！为任意骨骼装置协同生成3D动作与视频

paragraphs.en: 总结：NVIDIA提出可同时生成任意骨架的3D动作与视频的新模型，并自动恢复相机将动作嵌入3D场景，支持文本驱动动画与关键帧控制。 Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
paragraphs.zh: 总结：NVIDIA提出可同时生成任意骨架的3D动作与视频的新模型，并自动恢复相机将动作嵌入3D场景，支持文本驱动动画与关键帧控制。视频生成模型如今已能描绘极为逼真的运动。 然而尚不清楚如何超越像素来利用这些运动：即为特定的3D资产制作动画，并在其3D场景中回放该动画。 例如，视频模型可以展示一只猴子跳过横杆，但它无法将这一跳跃作为可回放的3D动作返回并放置到3D场景中。 在此，我们提出一个模型，可直接为任意提供的骨架共同生成视频与3D动作，并同时生成一个相机来将该动作配准到场景中。 此前的视频-动作模型要么仅处理人类骨架，且往往增加数十亿参数，要么从生成的2D姿态图通过三角测量得到3D动作。 我们则将3D动作保留在一个支持任意骨架的独立模型中，并通过少量交叉注意力层将其连接到预训练的视频模型。 这种分离使动作模型能够首先从纯动作数据中学习骨架如何运动，而这类数据比配对视频更易于获取和增强。 此外，我们的模型学会在视频帧中定位每个关节，这使我们能够恢复相机并将3D动作放置到场景中。 为了在多种骨架上进行训练，我们使用生成式视频编辑器将动画化的3D资产放置到适合其动作的场景中，并对编辑结果进行筛选，使其已知动作保持有效。 结合人类和机器人视频，这产生了近20万个训练对。 我们的评估表明，与以视频为先的流水线相比，我们的模型能更忠实地从文本为多种骨架制作动画，且其动作会对周围场景作出响应。 它还能将视频转换为骨架动作、将骨架动作转换为视频，并支持基于关键帧的3D动作控制。 视频及更多结果可在我们的项目页面获取：https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/。
